```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat

DOC = "PCMR-001"
UO_TITLE = "A-Mab Drug Substance"

# --- doc-local derived scalars: every one pulled from the model, never typed ------
steps_df = process_steps_df()
scope_df = char_scope_df()
n_steps = len(steps_df)
n_doe_steps = int((scope_df["Multivariate"] > 0).sum())
n_params = int(V["n_parameters"])
n_multivariate = int(scope_df["Multivariate"].sum())
n_univariate = int(scope_df["Univariate"].sum())

# classification
cc = class_counts()
n_cpp, n_wc_cpp, n_kpp, n_gpp = cc["CPP"], cc["WC-CPP"], cc["KPP"], cc["GPP"]
n_quality_linked = int(V["n_cpp"])          # CPP + WC-CPP
n_perf_params = n_kpp + n_gpp
cpp_row = param_reg[param_reg.classification == "CPP"].iloc[0]
cpp_nor_width = float(cpp_row.nor_high - cpp_row.nor_low)
cpp_char_width = float(cpp_row.par_high - cpp_row.par_low)
wc_bounded = param_reg[(param_reg.classification == "WC-CPP")
                       & (param_reg.study == "univariate")]
n_wc_bounded = len(wc_bounded)
n_ql_steps = int(param_reg[param_reg.classification.isin(["CPP", "WC-CPP"])]
                 .unit_operation.nunique())

# quality attributes and capability
outcome_df = cqa_outcome_df()
n_cqa = len(outcome_df)
n_met = int((outcome_df["Outcome"] == "met").sum())
n_set_bioreactor = int((cqa_reg.set_by == "bioreactor").sum())
n_viral_cqa = int((cqa_reg.category == "viral safety").sum())
n_ds_cqa = n_cqa - n_viral_cqa
n_glycan = int((cqa_reg.category == "glycosylation").sum())
capk = cap.set_index("key")
tightest = cap.loc[cap["Cpk"].idxmin()]
tightest_margin = float(tightest["mean"] - tightest["acc_low"])
hm = capk.loc["high_mannose"]
hm_margin = float(hm["mean"] - hm["acc_low"])
xm = capk.loc["lrv_xmulv"]
xm_margin = float(xm["mean"] - xm["acc_low"])
pa = capk.loc["leached_protein_a"]

# viral clearance
vc_df = viral_clearance_df()
vc_cum = vc_df[vc_df["Step"] == "Cumulative"].iloc[0]
vc_req = vc_df[vc_df["Step"] == "Requirement (drug substance)"].iloc[0]
n_viral_steps = len(vc_df) - 2
xmulv_margin = float(vc_cum["XMuLV LRF"] - vc_req["XMuLV LRF"])
mvm_margin = float(vc_cum["MVM LRF"] - vc_req["MVM LRF"])

# nominal-batch performance
psum = csv("process_summary.csv").set_index("step")
wf = yield_waterfall_df()
min_step_yield = float(wf["Step yield (%)"].min())
min_step_yield_uo = wf.loc[wf["Step yield (%)"].idxmin(), "Unit operation"]

# deviations
devs_df = dev_register_all()
n_dev = int(V["n_deviations"])
n_dev_retained = int((devs_df["Disposition"] == "retained").sum())
n_dev_reports = int(devs_df["Report"].nunique())
n_dev_equipment = int(csv("deviations.csv")["equipment"].notna().sum())

# analytical methods
meth = csv("dev_methods.csv")
n_methods = len(meth)
meth_rsd = meth[~meth["loq_unit"].str.contains("log10")]
worst_rsd = meth_rsd.loc[meth_rsd["precision_pct"].idxmax()]
worst_share = meth.loc[meth["variance_fraction"].idxmax()]
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

The A-Mab drug substance process is characterized and its control strategy is defined. The
`{python} n_steps` unit operations of the drug substance train, Steps 3–10, were each
studied under an approved plan and reported separately, and the work was executed on
qualified scale-down models at the sending site under the master plan PCMP-001 and the
pre-characterization risk assessment RA-001. The campaign supports the technology transfer
planned in PTP-001, and this report consolidates its results. It follows the lifecycle
approach to process validation [@fda2011] and the enhanced development approach of ICH Q8,
Q9 and Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11], and it takes the process model, the quality
attribute framework and the criticality framework from the A-Mab case study [@amab2009],
which is also the source of the risk methodology RA-001 applies.

The campaign carried `{python} n_params` process parameters into study, of which
`{python} n_quality_linked` are linked to a critical quality attribute and are held inside
the design space. Of those, `{python} n_cpp` parameter is classified as a critical process
parameter and `{python} n_wc_cpp` as well-controlled critical process parameters. The remaining
`{python} n_perf_params` are key or general process parameters, and they are controlled and
monitored because a consistent process is part of the control strategy, not because any of
them was shown to move a quality attribute. The single critical process parameter is the pH
of the low-pH viral inactivation hold (@sec-classification).

All `{python} n_cqa` drug substance quality attributes met their acceptance criteria.
Capability was estimated by simulating `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` commercial
batches, with every parameter varying about its set-point on a spread set by its normal
operating range, and no simulated batch produced a value outside a criterion
(@sec-outcomes). The lowest capability index in the set is
`{python} f"{V['min_cpk']:.2f}"`, for cumulative MVM clearance, whose simulated mean lies
`{python} f"{tightest_margin:.2f}"` log₁₀ above the required floor. The tightest of the
attributes the process itself forms is high mannose at `{python} f"{hm['Cpk']:.2f}"`, with
`{python} f"{hm_margin:.2f}"` percentage points between its simulated mean and the nearer
of its two limits.

Cumulative viral clearance exceeds its requirement for both model viruses.
The claim rests on `{python} n_viral_steps` steps with independent mechanisms of removal
or inactivation, and gives `{python} f"{vc_cum['XMuLV LRF']:.2f}"` log₁₀ for XMuLV
against a requirement of `{python} f"{vc_req['XMuLV LRF']:.2f}"`, and
`{python} f"{vc_cum['MVM LRF']:.2f}"` log₁₀ for MVM against
`{python} f"{vc_req['MVM LRF']:.2f}"`. No clearance is claimed for the Protein A step or
for the cation exchange step, so the cumulative figures are conservative to the extent of
whatever those two steps deliver.

The campaign recorded `{python} n_dev` deviations. Each was investigated and dispositioned
in the report for its step, and one of them invalidated a designed experiment. The first anion exchange execution ran on a load that was not representative
of routine material, so the affected screening and response surface designs were
re-executed in full on requalified load (PCR-008). Of the rest,
`{python} n_dev_retained` were retained with a bounded impact argument and one was
corrected by modelling and verification runs.

Two bounds apply to everything reported here. Capability, proven acceptable ranges and
viral clearance are estimated from qualified scale-down models with the parameters held
close to their set-points, so the edges of the design space have not been run at commercial
scale and nothing in this report describes the behaviour of the process there. Stage 2 has
not been executed, so this report presents no process performance qualification data and
makes no claim about the performance of any batch made at commercial scale.

# Introduction {#sec-intro}

## The campaign and its documents

The A-Mab drug substance process was characterized in a single campaign covering Steps
3–10, in which each unit operation was studied over ranges wider than its routine control
range so that the effect of every parameter on product quality and on process performance
could be measured and bounded. The scope of the work was fixed before execution by RA-001,
which assigned every parameter to a multivariate study, to a univariate assessment, or to
no study at all, and the common methods, the acceptance framework and the criticality
framework were fixed by PCMP-001. This report consolidates the results and states the
outcome against each requirement the drug substance has to meet.

The package is listed in @tbl-corpus, and three documents sit above the per-step work.
PTP-001 defines the transfer from the sending site to the receiving site and is the reason
the campaign exists, RA-001 sets the study scope, and PCMP-001 is the umbrella plan over
the `{python} n_steps` characterization plans. Each unit operation then carries a plan and
a report, numbered by process step. This report rolls those reports up. It does not repeat
their analyses, and where a figure here comes from one of them, that report is named.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(corpus_docs_md(DOC))
```

: The A-Mab drug substance document package. {#tbl-corpus}

## Scope of the characterization

`{python} n_params` process parameters were carried into study, of which
`{python} n_multivariate` were studied in multivariate designs and
`{python} n_univariate` were assessed one at a time, and @tbl-scope gives the split by step
together with the plan and report that cover it. Of the `{python} n_steps` steps,
`{python} n_doe_steps` carried a designed experiment with a screening stage followed by a
response surface stage. Harvest and clarification (Step 4) and the ultrafiltration and
diafiltration step (Step 10) carried none, because neither step forms a product quality
attribute, and both were characterized univariately with reports that are correspondingly
shorter.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(scope_df)
```

: Characterization scope by unit operation, with the covering plan and report. {#tbl-scope}

The division of labour between the two design stages is the same at every step that has
one. The screening design identifies which parameters have an effect on which response,
and the response surface model is the predictive model, which makes it the basis of the
design space and of the proven acceptable ranges reported in each unit operation report.
Nothing in this report rests on a screening fit.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The campaign follows the lifecycle approach to process validation, in which Stage 1
establishes the process design and the commercial process is then qualified in Stage 2
[@fda2011]. The enhanced development approach of ICH Q8 was used throughout, so that prior
knowledge and risk assessment identify what matters, characterization bounds it, and the
result is a control strategy [@ichq8]. Criticality is treated as a continuum and not as a
binary label, following ICH Q9 [@ichq9]. The classification decisions follow the
development and manufacturing principles of ICH Q11 [@ichq11]. Viral safety is evaluated
under ICH Q5A, which is the basis of the modular clearance claim in @sec-viral [@ichq5a],
and the transfer to the receiving site is managed under the pharmaceutical quality system
of ICH Q10 [@ichq10] and planned in PTP-001.

# Process description and performance {#sec-process}

## The process train

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody produced by fed-batch cell culture and
purified on a platform train. Culture in the production bioreactor is followed by harvest
and clarification, Protein A capture, a low-pH viral inactivation hold, cation exchange
polishing, anion exchange polishing in flow-through mode, small-virus retentive filtration,
and ultrafiltration and diafiltration into the formulation buffer. @tbl-train lists the
steps with the role
each has in the control strategy, and @fig-flow shows the same train with the principal
quality impact of each step.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(steps_df)
```

: The A-Mab drug substance process train and the role of each step. {#tbl-train}

![The drug substance process train, with the principal quality impact of each unit operation.](../outputs/figures/fig_process_flow.png){#fig-flow width=100%}

The quality burden is not spread evenly across the train. The production bioreactor sets
`{python} n_set_bioreactor` of the `{python} n_cqa` quality attributes, which is more than
any other step (@tbl-cqa-scope). Cation exchange is the principal aggregate polishing step,
and anion exchange and virus filtration together carry the small-virus clearance claim. The
low-pH hold sets the enveloped-virus clearance claim (@sec-viral) and carries the only
critical process parameter in the process (@sec-classification). The remaining steps are
recovery, capture and formulation operations, and their parameters act on yield, on the
impurity burden or on the physical condition of the pool. Capture is also the step at which
leached Protein A enters the pool (@tbl-cqa-scope).

## Nominal batch performance

The nominal batch is the run at set-point that each report describes, and it is the
reference point for the ranges studied around it. Culture at
`{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,} L"` delivers a harvest titre of
`{python} f"{V['nominal_titer_g_per_l']:.2f}"` g/L at a final viability of
`{python} f"{V['final_viability_pct']:.1f}"`%, with a peak viable cell concentration of
`{python} f"{V['peak_vcd_e6']:.1f} e6 cells/mL"`. The drug substance is delivered at
`{python} f"{V['ds_conc_g_per_l']:.0f}"` g/L, and a batch yields
`{python} f"{V['ds_mass_kg']:.1f}"` kg at the end of the train.

Product yield across the train is given in @tbl-yield and plotted in @fig-yield. The
cumulative yield is `{python} pct(V['overall_yield'])` and the lowest single-step yield is
`{python} f"{min_step_yield:.1f}"`% at the cation exchange step. Yield is a process
performance attribute and not a quality attribute, so no step yield is an acceptance
criterion. The parameters that govern it are classified as key process parameters
(@sec-classification).

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(wf, floatfmt=[".0f", "", ".1f", ".1f"])
```

: Step and cumulative product yield across the drug substance train. {#tbl-yield}

![Cumulative product yield across the eight modelled unit operations.](../outputs/figures/fig_yield_waterfall.png){#fig-yield width=90%}

The purification train reduces the impurity burden by several orders of magnitude. In the
nominal batch, host cell protein leaves the capture step at
`{python} f"{psum.loc[5, 'pool_hcp_ng_mg']:,.0f}"` ng/mg, falls to
`{python} f"{psum.loc[7, 'hcp_out_ng_mg']:,.0f}"` ng/mg across cation exchange and to
`{python} f"{psum.loc[8, 'hcp_out_ng_mg']:.1f}"` ng/mg across anion exchange. Leached
Protein A enters the pool at the capture step at
`{python} f"{psum.loc[5, 'leached_protein_a_ppm']:.2f}"` ppm and is then cleared by the
same two ion exchange steps. Aggregate rises across the low-pH hold, by
`{python} f"{psum.loc[6, 'aggregate_delta_pct']:.2f}"` percentage points in the nominal
batch, and is reduced `{python} f"{psum.loc[7, 'aggregate_clearance_fold']:.1f}"`-fold at
cation exchange, which is why that step is described as the principal aggregate polish.

# Consolidated quality attribute outcomes {#sec-outcomes}

## The attributes and where they are set

The drug substance has `{python} n_cqa` critical quality attributes, and every one of them
met its acceptance criterion in the characterized process. @tbl-cqa-scope lists the
register with the criticality of each attribute, the step that sets it and the report that
characterizes it. Of the `{python} n_cqa` attributes, `{python} n_viral_cqa` are cumulative
viral clearance claims delivered by several steps together, and the remaining
`{python} n_ds_cqa` are product quality or process impurity attributes measured on the drug
substance itself.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqa_scope_df())
```

: The drug substance quality attribute register, with the step that sets each attribute and the report that characterizes it. {#tbl-cqa-scope}

Setting an attribute and controlling it are different things, and for several attributes
they happen at different steps. Host cell protein and residual DNA are generated in the
culture and are cleared by Protein A capture (PCR-005), cation exchange (PCR-007) and anion
exchange (PCR-008). Aggregate is formed in the bioreactor (PCR-003), rises across the
low-pH hold (PCR-006) and is reduced at cation exchange (PCR-007), the principal polishing
step for it. Leached Protein A is formed at the capture step (PCR-005) and is cleared by
the two ion exchange steps. The `{python} n_glycan` glycan attributes are formed inside the
cell and in the culture fluid. The platform purification steps do not separate
glycosylation variants of a monoclonal antibody [@amab2009], so PCR-003 carries them alone.
Acidic charge variants are also set in the culture, and the low-pH hold reports them as a
response as well (PCR-006).

## Outcome against the acceptance criteria

@tbl-cqa-outcome gives the outcome of the campaign attribute by attribute, and each row
compares the simulated commercial-scale distribution with the criterion that governs the
attribute. For the impurity, size variant and charge variant attributes only the upper
limit is an acceptance limit, so the criterion is one-sided and the capability index in
@tbl-cap is one-sided with it. For the viral clearance attributes the criterion is a floor, and for the
glycan attributes both limits apply. Across `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` simulated
batches, `{python} n_met` attributes met their criterion and none produced a value outside
it.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(outcome_df)
```

: Simulated commercial-scale outcome for every drug substance quality attribute. {#tbl-cqa-outcome}

Two rows repay a second look. The simulated range for acidic charge variants extends below
the lower figure shown for that attribute in @tbl-cqa-scope, which is not an acceptance
limit, because the specification for acidic charge variants is one-sided and the risk it
addresses is an elevated level. The second is leached Protein A, whose simulated
concentrations lie far below the limit, so its capability index is correspondingly large
and carries no information beyond that.

The margins are not uniform. High mannose and the two viral clearance attributes sit
closest to their limits, and they are the attributes on which the operating region is
effectively binding, with the capability figures given in @sec-capability. The impurity
attributes clear their limits by a wide margin, which is a property of a train in which
the capture step and both polishing steps remove them, and not a property of any single
step.

The outcome in each row is a simulated one. The simulation varies the process parameters and
propagates them through the fitted models of the scale-down studies, so it covers the
variation those models describe and no other, and it does not cover raw material
variability beyond what the models carry. It is not a measurement of commercial equipment,
and the attribute levels are confirmed at scale during Stage 2.

# Parameter classification summary {#sec-classification}

## The classification across the train

Every parameter carried into the campaign has a classification, and the counts are
`{python} n_cpp` critical process parameter, `{python} n_wc_cpp` well-controlled critical
process parameters, `{python} n_kpp` key process parameters and `{python} n_gpp` general
process parameters. @fig-class shows how they fall across the train. @tbl-cpp lists the
`{python} n_quality_linked` quality-linked parameters with their set-points and normal
operating ranges, and those ranges are the ranges the commercial process is asked to hold.
The classification decisions are made in the report for each step, under SOP-4001.

![Post-characterization classification of process parameters by unit operation.](../outputs/figures/fig_param_classification.png){#fig-class width=100%}

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cpp_params())
```

: The quality-linked process parameters of the drug substance train, with their set-points and normal operating ranges. {#tbl-cpp}

The distinction between the two quality-linked classes is the risk of leaving the design
space and not the size of the effect [@amab2009]. A well-controlled critical process
parameter affects a critical quality attribute and has a low risk of moving outside the
design space, whereas a critical process parameter carries a high risk of it. The class
therefore follows from the control capability of the equipment as much as from the result
of the study. The `{python} n_wc_cpp` well-controlled critical process parameters are spread across
`{python} n_ql_steps` unit operations, and every one of them is held within a normal
operating range that lies at or inside the edges of the range characterized for it. The
characterized range is given parameter by parameter in the report for each step.

## The exceptions

The process has `{python} n_cpp` critical process parameter, the pH of the low-pH viral
inactivation hold. Its normal operating range is `{python} f"{cpp_nor_width:.1f}"` pH units
wide, and the study characterized `{python} f"{cpp_char_width:.1f}"` pH units around it. The
parameter governs the enveloped-virus clearance claim, an attribute of very high criticality
(@tbl-cqa-scope), which satisfies the first half of the definition. The second half is a
judgement about how closely the step can be held to its range, and the assessment behind it
is in PCR-006, which also records the classification. No other step needed the more
stringent class.

The campaign classified `{python} n_wc_bounded` quality-linked parameter on a univariate
assessment and not on a multivariate effect estimate. It is the operating flow rate of the anion
exchange step, which RA-001 assigned to a univariate assessment and which PCR-008 then
classified from the range given in @tbl-cpp, so its classification rests on a bounding
argument and not on a measured multivariate effect.

Neither harvest and clarification nor the formulation step carries a quality-linked
parameter (@fig-class). Neither step sets a critical quality attribute (@tbl-cqa-scope), so
their parameters are classified for process performance. The ranges they are held to
protect yield, filter capacity and the concentration of the delivered pool.

## Null results and what they are worth

A parameter that produced no measurable effect over the range studied is still classified,
and the range over which nothing happened is recorded in the report for its step.
On that basis `{python} n_gpp` parameters are classified as general process parameters. The absence of an
effect over a characterized range is evidence that the attribute is robust to the parameter
over that range, but it is not evidence about conditions outside it. Each report states the
range it covered.

# Process capability {#sec-capability}

Commercial-scale capability was estimated for every drug substance quality attribute, and
the lowest capability index in the set is `{python} f"{V['min_cpk']:.2f}"`. The estimate
comes from simulating `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches, in which each batch
draws every process parameter about its set-point, with a spread set by the width of its
normal operating range and bounded by the range characterized, and propagates the drawn
operating point through the fitted models of the scale-down studies. Capability is one-sided
against the governing limit for the impurity, size variant and charge variant attributes
and for the clearance attributes (@tbl-cap), and two-sided for the glycan attributes.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cap_for(list(cqa_reg["key"])), floatfmt=".2f")
```

: Commercial-scale process capability for every drug substance quality attribute. {#tbl-cap}

![Simulated drug substance attribute distributions against their acceptance limits, annotated with the capability index.](../outputs/figures/fig_capability.png){#fig-cap width=100%}

The tightest capability in the process is cumulative MVM clearance, at
`{python} f"{tightest['Cpk']:.2f}"`, with a simulated mean
`{python} f"{tightest_margin:.2f}"` log₁₀ above its floor, and cumulative XMuLV clearance
is next, at `{python} f"{xm['Cpk']:.2f}"` with a margin of
`{python} f"{xm_margin:.2f}"` log₁₀. Both are governed by more than one step, so neither
figure is the property of a single unit operation, and the contributions are set out in
@sec-viral. High mannose is the tightest of the attributes formed in the process, at
`{python} f"{hm['Cpk']:.2f}"`, and it is governed by the bioreactor alone (PCR-003). The
remaining attributes clear their limits by a wider margin, and the largest index in
@tbl-cap, for leached Protein A, reflects a pool concentration far below the limit and
nothing else.

This report sets no acceptance threshold for the capability index, and each index is
reported with the margin between the simulated mean and the governing limit, which is the
quantity a control decision acts on.

The capability estimate is built on qualified scale-down models and
inherits their assumptions about feed states and about scale independence. It describes the
process operating near its set-points, so it says nothing about performance at the edges of
the design space, which have not been run at commercial scale. It is not a
measurement of the commercial process at all, and it is confirmed during Stage 2, when
capability is re-estimated from process performance qualification batches and from the data
of continued process verification.

# Viral clearance summary {#sec-viral}

## The modular claim

Cumulative viral clearance exceeds its requirement for both model viruses.
@tbl-viral gives the credited log reduction of each contributing step, the cumulative
total and the requirement, and @fig-viral shows the same figures against the requirement
line. The claim is modular in the sense of ICH Q5A, which means that each step was spiked
and studied independently on a qualified small-scale model and the step increments are then
added [@ichq5a]. The model viruses are XMuLV (an enveloped retrovirus) and MVM (a small non-enveloped
parvovirus chosen as the worst case for physical removal).

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(vc_df, floatfmt=".2f")
```

: Modular viral clearance by credited step, in log10 reduction, against the drug substance requirement. {#tbl-viral}

![Modular viral clearance by credited step for both model viruses, against the requirement.](../outputs/figures/fig_viral_clearance.png){#fig-viral width=100%}

@tbl-viral credits `{python} n_viral_steps` steps. The low-pH hold contributes
`{python} f"{vc_df.loc[0, 'XMuLV LRF']:.2f}"` log₁₀ of XMuLV clearance and is the largest
single contribution to the enveloped-virus claim (PCR-006), and it contributes nothing to
the MVM claim, which @tbl-viral records as zero, because a parvovirus has no lipid envelope
for low pH to act on. Anion exchange contributes
`{python} f"{vc_df.loc[1, 'MVM LRF']:.2f}"` log₁₀ of MVM clearance in flow-through mode
(PCR-008) and virus filtration contributes
`{python} f"{vc_df.loc[2, 'MVM LRF']:.2f}"` log₁₀ (PCR-009), so the two together carry the
small-virus claim, and the margins over the requirement are
`{python} f"{xmulv_margin:.2f}"` log₁₀ for XMuLV and `{python} f"{mvm_margin:.2f}"` log₁₀
for MVM.

## Orthogonality, and what is not claimed

Adding the step increments is only defensible if the mechanisms are independent, and the
three mechanisms differ. Low pH inactivates by disrupting the viral envelope, anion exchange
partitions virus from product by charge in a step where the product flows through and the
impurities bind, and virus filtration removes by size on a membrane rated for small
non-enveloped viruses. A condition that reduces one of the three increments is therefore not
expected to reduce the others. The campaign did not study conditions that act on more than
one step at once, so that expectation rests on the mechanisms and not on a cross-step
experiment.

No clearance is claimed for the Protein A step or for the cation exchange step, and
neither contributes to the totals in @tbl-viral. Neither step was studied for viral
clearance in this campaign, so the cumulative claim is conservative to the extent of
whatever those two steps deliver.

The log reduction values come from spiking
studies on small-scale models and are not measurements of the commercial process. Each
step's contribution holds over the ranges that step characterized, and the constraints are
step specific, covering pH, hold time and temperature at the low-pH hold (PCR-006), load pH
and conductivity at anion exchange (PCR-008), and volumetric load at virus filtration
(PCR-009), where clearance falls as the load rises. The clearance attributes in @tbl-cap
carry a simulated mean that differs from the nominal totals in @tbl-viral, because the
capability estimate varies the process parameters and the nominal batch does not.

# Overall control strategy {#sec-control}

## What the control strategy has to do

The control strategy has two purposes. The first is to assure product quality and patient
safety, and it does that by holding every quality-linked parameter inside the design space
established by the characterization studies. The second is to assure that the commercial
process runs consistently, and it does that by controlling the key process parameters and
by monitoring the process attributes that report on the health of a batch. The two
purposes need different evidence, which is why a key process parameter is controlled even
though it was shown not to move a quality attribute [@amab2009].

## Parameter control

The quality-linked parameters and their normal operating ranges are given in @tbl-cpp, each
is controlled to that range in routine manufacture, and each range sits inside the region
the characterization studies covered. Movement inside the design space is not a regulatory
change [@ichq8], but it is still assessed prospectively under the quality system before it
is made [@ichq10], and movement outside the characterized region is a change and is handled
through change control.

The critical process parameter, the pH of the low-pH hold, carries the tightest control
requirement in the process, and its control is defined in PCR-006. The proven acceptable
ranges that support each parameter's range are reported per step and per attribute in the
report for that step, and are not reproduced here.

## In-process control and monitoring

In-process controls are placed where an attribute can be measured early enough to act on
it. Post-clarification turbidity is monitored at the harvest step and is one of the
parameters that step controls (PCR-004). Pool host cell protein is measured after each
chromatography step (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008), and pool aggregate after the low-pH
hold and the cation exchange step,
which is what makes the clearance chain described in @sec-process auditable batch by batch.
The pH and the duration of the low-pH hold are recorded against the batch record, and the
integrity test after virus filtration is a release-relevant control on the small-virus
claim. The concentration of the final pool is verified before the drug substance is
dispensed.

## Release testing

Release testing confirms on the batch what process control is designed to deliver. The
`{python} n_ds_cqa` product quality and process impurity attributes in @tbl-cqa-outcome are
measured on the drug substance and compared with the criterion given there, so each of them
is confirmed batch by batch once the process has run. The `{python} n_viral_cqa` viral
clearance attributes are not confirmed in that way, because no test on the drug substance
measures them. They are process claims established on spiked small-scale models
(@sec-viral), and they are held by the operating ranges of the
`{python} n_viral_steps` credited steps and by the in-process controls above. A release
result arrives after the batch has been made, so testing at release cannot by itself control
an attribute [@ichq8]. For this reason the control strategy places the burden on the
parameter ranges and the in-process controls, and uses release testing to confirm the
outcome.

## Analytical control

Every attribute in @tbl-cqa-outcome is measured by a validated method. @tbl-methods
summarises the validated performance of `{python} n_methods` of the methods the campaign
relies on, most of which measure a drug substance quality attribute. Turbidity and protein
concentration are in that table for a different reason, because turbidity is an in-process
control at the harvest step (PCR-004) and protein concentration governs the pool the
formulation step delivers (PCR-010). Method performance matters to the control strategy for
two reasons. It sets how much of the observed variation belongs to the process instead of
to the measurement, and it sets how small a change the process can be held to.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(method_perf_df(precision_with_unit=True))
```

: Validated performance of the analytical methods the campaign relies on. {#tbl-methods}

The least precise method of those reported as a relative standard deviation is the host
cell protein assay, at `{python} f"{worst_rsd['precision_pct']:g}"`% RSD, and the largest
share of observed variation attributable to a method is
`{python} f"{worst_share['variance_fraction']:.2f}"`, for the leached Protein A assay.
Neither limits the control strategy, because both attributes clear their limits by a wide
margin (@tbl-cqa-outcome). The two infectivity assays are reported as a log10 standard
deviation and not as a relative standard deviation, so their precision figures are not
comparable with the rest of the table. Methods that do not appear in @tbl-methods carry
their validated performance in their own method validation reports. @tbl-sop lists the
controlled documents the unit operation studies cite from harvest onward, and the culture
operation and analytical procedures the bioreactor study works to are cited in PCR-003.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(all_sop_table())
```

: Controlled documents cited by the unit operation studies from harvest onward (Steps 4–10). {#tbl-sop}

## Life-cycle and feed-input controls

Three life-cycle controls sit behind the ranges in @tbl-cpp. Chromatography resins are
managed for cycle life, packing and sanitization under SOP-2008. The clearance and
polishing performance of a column is a function of its history as well as of its operating
conditions. The virus retentive filter is integrity tested after use under SOP-2012, and
the analytical methods transfer to the receiving site and are re-qualified there under the
plan in PTP-001.

One feed-input control follows from a deviation. The first anion exchange execution used a
load that had been held neutralized for
`{python} f"{dev_008_01_neutralized_hold_h:.0f}"` hours, which raised its acidic charge
variant content well above the level of routine material (@sec-deviations). The time the
neutralized cation exchange pool is held before anion exchange loading is therefore treated
as a control input for that step, and PCR-008 carries the assessment.

## What the control strategy does not cover

The strategy described here covers the drug substance process from Step 3 to Step 10. It
does not cover the seed train ahead of the production bioreactor, the cell bank, the raw
material controls or the drug product process. All of those are described elsewhere in the
application. It does not by itself show that the commercial process is in a state of
control, which is the purpose of Stage 2 and of the continued process verification that
follows it.

# Deviations across the campaign {#sec-deviations}

The campaign recorded `{python} n_dev` deviations across the `{python} n_dev_reports` unit
operation studies, and one of them invalidated a designed experiment. @tbl-dev gives the
register with the route by which each was detected and its disposition. The investigation,
the root cause and the impact assessment for each are in the report named in the register,
and are not repeated here.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(devs_df)
```

: Deviations recorded across the characterization campaign. {#tbl-dev}

## The deviation that invalidated a study

The most serious deviation is DEV-008-01. The load used in the first anion exchange
execution carried
`{python} f"{dev_008_01_acidic_variants_deamidated_pct:.1f}"`% acidic charge variants,
against `{python} f"{dev_008_01_acidic_variants_requalified_pct:.1f}"`% in the
requalified load, after the neutralized cation exchange eluate was held for
`{python} f"{dev_008_01_neutralized_hold_h:.0f}"` hours. A load in that condition is not
representative of routine material, so the screening and response surface designs executed
on it were invalidated for the purpose of defining an operating region, and both were
re-executed in full on requalified load. The analysis reported in PCR-008 is the
re-execution, and the first execution is retained there as a superseded dataset and
referenced to confirm the root cause. No part of it is analysed in this report.

One further deviation at the same step was closed by analysis instead of by re-execution.
The trailing-edge collection set-point used for the flow-through pool was more permissive
than intended in both executions, at
`{python} f"{dev_008_02_uv_pool_stop_original_mau:.0f}"` mAU against a corrected
`{python} f"{dev_008_02_uv_pool_stop_corrected_mau:.0f}"` mAU. The effect on the pool was
modelled and then checked against `{python} f"{dev_008_02_ver_n:.0f}"` verification runs,
and PCR-008 gives the assessment.

## The retained deviations

In `{python} n_dev_retained` cases the deviation was retained, which means the affected data
were kept in the analysis with an argument that bounds the impact. Most fall into three kinds. Some
are single-run excursions of a controlled parameter that stayed inside the range the study
itself covered. The pressure excursion at virus filtration (DEV-009-01) and the
transmembrane pressure excursion at the formulation step (DEV-010-01) are of that kind.
Some are material events found before or after execution, such as the expired buffer lot at
cation exchange (DEV-007-01) and the buffer released below its pH acceptance range at anion
exchange (DEV-008-03). Others are analytical events resolved by re-test or by dilution,
such as the cytotoxicity seen at low dilution in the XMuLV infectivity assay (DEV-006-02).
The remainder are single events of other kinds. The dissolved carbon dioxide probe drift
(DEV-003-01) and the feed under-delivery on a centre-point batch (DEV-003-02) are both
bioreactor events. The others are the hold-time record discrepancy between the control
system and the manual log at the low-pH hold (DEV-006-01) and the final pool concentration
below target at the formulation step (DEV-010-02), which was corrected by topping up.

Most of the deviations in @tbl-dev were found by checks that run independently of the study
analysis, among them buffer release testing, in-process monitoring, equipment history
review, pre-use verification and post-execution reconciliation. The exceptions are
analytical events. The leached Protein A result that fell out of trend at the capture step
(DEV-005-02) and the assay cytotoxicity at the low-pH hold (DEV-006-02) were both found in
the review of the study's own results. An instrumented scale-down system is involved in
`{python} n_dev_equipment` of the deviations. Those systems
are listed in @tbl-equipment with their calibration status at the time the affected studies
ran, and each was inside its calibration interval.

```{python}
#| output: asis

```

: Instrumented scale-down systems under calibration and change control. {#tbl-equipment}

# Conclusions and Stage 2 readiness {#sec-conclusions}

The A-Mab drug substance process is characterized across Steps 3–10 and the campaign
supports a defined control strategy. Every one of the `{python} n_params` process
parameters has a classification, `{python} n_quality_linked` of them are quality-linked and
are controlled to the ranges in @tbl-cpp, and the remaining `{python} n_perf_params` are
controlled for process consistency. Each unit operation has a plan, a report and an
operating region. At the `{python} n_doe_steps` steps that carried a designed experiment
the operating region is derived from that step's response surface models, and at harvest
and the formulation step it rests on the univariate assessments those reports present.

Every drug substance quality attribute met its acceptance criterion in the simulated
commercial process. The lowest capability index is `{python} f"{V['min_cpk']:.2f}"`, for
cumulative MVM clearance, and the tightest of the attributes the process forms is high
mannose at `{python} f"{hm['Cpk']:.2f}"`. Cumulative viral clearance exceeds the
requirement by `{python} f"{xmulv_margin:.2f}"` log₁₀ for XMuLV and by
`{python} f"{mvm_margin:.2f}"` log₁₀ for MVM, on `{python} n_viral_steps` steps with
independent mechanisms. The campaign recorded `{python} n_dev` deviations, one of which
forced a study to be re-executed in full, and each was dispositioned in the report for its
step.

The capability and clearance figures are estimated on qualified scale-down models and are
not measured on commercial equipment, and they describe the process operating near its
set-points, so they say nothing about the edges of the design space, which have not been
run at scale. The viral clearance values come from small-scale spiking studies. Nothing
here rests on a screening model, and no proven acceptable range extends beyond the range
its step characterized.

What remains is Stage 2. The process transfers to the receiving site under PTP-001, process
performance qualification batches are executed there, capability is re-estimated from those
batches instead of from simulation, and the analytical methods transfer and are re-qualified
at the receiving site. Continued process verification then runs for the life of the
product. This report does not qualify the commercial process, and it makes no claim about
the performance of any batch made at commercial scale.
